name: Keerai Masiyal
subtitle: soft mashed greens with dal and a garlic tempering, the everyday rice-plate side

ingredients.note: arai keerai; spinach works if you cannot find it
softens faster and helps the mash
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Pick the leaves off the thick stalks and wash them in three changes of water — amaranth carries grit.
Soak the toor dal 20 minutes if your cooker runs fast; it should collapse completely, not hold its shape.

steps.text: Pressure cook the toor dal and moong dal with turmeric and 300ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own.
Meanwhile boil the greens in 100ml water with a pinch of salt, uncovered, for 5 minutes until they wilt to a quarter of their volume.
steps.tip: Cook the greens uncovered — a lid traps the acid and turns them army green.

steps.text: Mash the cooked dal with the back of a ladle until smooth.
Tip the greens and their liquid into the dal and mash together with a wooden masher for a minute. It should be thick and spoonable, not soupy.
Simmer 5 minutes over low heat, seasoning with salt.
For the tempering, heat the sesame oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, red chillies and crushed garlic.
steps.tip: Wait for the mustard to pop before anything else goes in, or the seeds turn bitter rather than nutty.

steps.text: Fry until the garlic is golden at the edges, about 90 seconds, then stir in the asafoetida off the heat.
Pour the tempering over the masiyal, stir once and serve with hot rice and a spoon of sesame oil.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat gently with a splash of water; the greens dull in colour but the flavour deepens. Do not freeze — the mash goes watery.
